biography: Sandro Sanches, a name now synonymous with the raw, untamed spirit of Brazilian stock car racing, didn't grow up dreaming of checkered flags. He grew up smelling burning rubber and exhaust fumes in his father's small-town mechanic shop in Minas Gerais. His father, a former amateur racer himself, instilled in Sandro a love for the Opala, a classic Brazilian car that would later become Sandro's chariot. Sandro's first 'race' was an impromptu sprint down a dirt road against a rival mechanic, a race he won with a combination of skill and reckless abandon. This victory, witnessed by a small crowd of cheering locals, ignited a fire in Sandro that couldn't be extinguished. He started competing in local Opala races, quickly gaining a reputation for his aggressive driving style and unpredictable temperament. While he achieved podium finishes, his inconsistency often cost him championships. Sandro's career reached a turning point when he secured a spot in the prestigious Opala Old Stock Race series. Now, at 28, Sandro is considered to be in his prime, battling for wins against seasoned veterans and hungry newcomers alike. He remains a captivating, albeit inconsistent, force on the track, thrilling fans with his daring overtakes and fiery personality.
drivingStyle: Sandro's driving style is best described as 'controlled chaos.' He attacks corners with a ferocity that often leaves spectators breathless, pushing the limits of grip and daring to brake later than anyone else on the grid. Tire management is not his forte; he prefers to extract every last ounce of performance from his tires early in a stint, often sacrificing long-run pace. Under pressure, Sandro can either crumble spectacularly or rise to the occasion, delivering masterful performances when the stakes are highest. His inconsistency makes him a thrilling, but unpredictable, competitor.

rivalries.name: Ricardo 'The Professor' Oliveira
rivalries.reason: A veteran of the series, Oliveira represents everything Sandro is not: calm, calculating, and consistent. Their contrasting styles often lead to tense battles on track and clashes off track, fueled by Oliveira's condescending attitude towards Sandro's aggressive approach.

rivalries.name: Isabela 'The Hurricane' Costa
rivalries.reason: Isabela is a young, talented driver who shares Sandro's aggressive driving style, but with more control. Their rivalry is based on mutual respect and a desire to prove who is the fastest of the new generation of Brazilian racers. Their on-track battles are always intense and unpredictable.

rivalries.name: Joaquim 'The Rock' Barbosa
rivalries.reason: Joaquim's unyielding defense and refusal to yield on track frustrates Sandro immensely. Sandro sees Joaquim's defensive style as cowardly, while Joaquim views Sandro's aggressive moves as dangerous and reckless, leading to frequent clashes and complaints.

quirks: Always wears the same faded blue t-shirt under his racing suit, claiming it brings him luck.
Listens to a specific classic Brazilian rock song right before every race to pump himself up.
Has to tap the roof of his Opala three times before getting in, a ritual he started after a near-miss accident early in his career.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't about being smooth; it's about dancing on the edge of disaster. If you're not scared, you're not going fast enough!"
careerHighlight: Winning the 2022 Interlagos Old Stock Race after starting from the back of the grid. He overtook 15 cars in the final 10 laps with a series of daring maneuvers, solidifying his reputation as a fearless racer.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the 2021 Curitiba race while leading on the last lap. The crash was caused by his own over-aggressiveness, costing him a crucial victory and damaging his reputation.
